Original work of the Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible available at https://github.com/openscriptures/morphhb.

Lexical files: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible Project. Morphology and lexical files are used under CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) and adapted here into word spans, grammar cues and source notes. The Hebrew text is public domain. No endorsement is implied.

Greek text: Nestle 1904 (public domain). Morphology and lemmas: Ulrik Sandborg-Petersen and biblicalhumanities.org (CC0). English glosses: Berean Interlinear Bible, via biblicalhumanities.org; see the public-domain terms (https://berean.bible/terms.htm).
Hebrew verse readings, including the sound of verse videos, are by Rabbi Dan Be’eri, under CC BY-SA 3.0. Each verse’s exact credit and license are in its Sources.
This is the preserved source text, without teaching dots, superscripts or icon placeholders. Select it to copy.

Root and lemma are different. A traditional lexical relationship is not a claim of certain historical origin. Illustrations are learning aids; the original text and its sourced morphology guide the reading.

The Greek text and grammar follow the Nestle 1904 morphology source. English word meanings are from the Berean Interlinear Bible; they are word glosses in the original word order, not a sentence translation.
Small marks, useful clues. The colors, numbers and letters are Hinneh teaching conventions.

Grammar explanations adapt unfoldingWord Hebrew Grammar, © 2021 unfoldingWord, under %1$s. They are condensed and reworded; the adapted explanations are shared under the same license. The numeric and letter codes, colors and layout are Hinneh’s teaching conventions. No endorsement is implied.

Word meanings are glosses in the original word order, not a sentence translation. Hebrew meanings are the approved word glosses from Global Bible Tools. Where the sources do not line up word for word, the meaning is left out rather than guessed.
Lemmas and grammar follow the Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible; the grammar descriptions are generated from its codes. Many words do not have a reviewed root yet, so no root is shown for them.
A general word picture is a memory aid for the word; a particular verse may call for a different picture.

Hinneh’s pictures, videos, word recordings and synthesized verse readings are AI-generated study aids, still awaiting review. Hebrew verse readings by Rabbi Dan Be’eri are human recordings, used under CC BY-SA 3.0. The original text and its sources guide the reading. To report a problem with a picture, open its verse on hinneh.us.
